requirement: Immediate/deferred delivery and callback hits remain correct

inputs.name: default
inputs.call: fresh process: godot --headless --path . --script driver.gd (direct emit, then deferred emit, then one awaited process_frame)

obligations.note: _on_direct() body -- fires synchronously, inside the emit() call on line 17, before line 18 runs; the interleaving is only provable via expected_log_sequence, not this obligation alone
_on_deferred() body -- reached by process end, since the frame does turn in this run; whether it fired before or after the post-emit line is, again, only provable via the log, not this obligation

inputs.name: deferred_never_flushed
inputs.call: fresh process: godot --headless --path . --script driver.gd -- no_flush (quits immediately after the deferred emit, before any frame turns)

obligations.note: genuinely never reached in this run's own process: the frame never turns before quit(), so the deferred callback never fires. This is the real discriminating obligation -- a tool that treats CONNECT_DEFERRED delivery as synchronous would show this as a false_hit.

run_deferred() itself runs to completion, including line 24 -- emit() returns synchronously even for a deferred connection, it's only the CALLBACK delivery (line 12) that's queued, not the emit() call itself

notes: Both inputs are their own fresh process (per the F041 precedent): a single cumulative coverage report can only show whichever facts are true by process end, so 'the deferred callback never fired' can only be expressed by a process in which nothing ever delivers it, not by an intermediate snapshot inside a longer-running process. Mechanism corrected 2026-09-19 by the independent second-reviewer pass: the original note (and driver.gd's comment) said the callback never fires in deferred_never_flushed because 'the frame never turns before quit()'. That is not why. quit() only requests exit, and Godot still runs one main-loop iteration -- including a MessageQueue flush -- before honoring it (demonstrated on F048, where a call_deferred() on a tree node DOES run after a quit() issued from _initialize()). Line 12 stays unreached here for a different reason: deferred_subject is a RefCounted held only by a local in _initialize(), so it is freed when _initialize() returns, before the flush, and the queued signal delivery has no live target. Verified by instrumenting _on_deferred() with a print(): with the fixture as bound, the print never appears in no_flush mode; with deferred_subject additionally held in a driver member variable, it DOES appear after the driver's own prints. The negative obligation on line 12 is therefore correct for this fixture exactly as bound, but it depends on the subject's lifetime, not on frame timing -- any change that keeps the subject alive past _initialize() would make it false. default's obligations are all true and carry no discriminating power at the coverage level by themselves -- expected_log_sequence (fixture-specific, checked by the driver, not pilot/harness/comparator.py, same category as F013/F042's expected_log) is what actually proves the synchronous-vs-queued distinction for that run. deferred_never_flushed is what gives this fixture real coverage-level discriminating power, the same role F041's zero_instances input plays: a tool that (incorrectly) delivers CONNECT_DEFERRED callbacks synchronously would show a false_hit on line 12 in this run. Confirmed on the pinned Godot 4.7.1 engine via this fixture's own driver.gd.
author: godot-tooling-session-2026-09-19
reviewer: independent review agent (fable), 2026-09-19: re-hashed subject.gd, checked all 10 obligation line numbers against source, and re-ran both inputs on the pinned engine with an instrumented copy of subject.gd (print() inside _on_deferred). The line-12 negative claim reproduces exactly as bound, but the stated mechanism was wrong: a frame does turn after quit() (see F048's correction); the callback is undelivered because the RefCounted target is freed when _initialize() returns. Corrected the notes and driver.gd's comment; no obligation changed.
ambiguities: The deferred_never_flushed negative depends on deferred_subject being freed before the post-quit() flush (it is a local RefCounted). A fixture wanting 'queued delivery never happens' independent of target lifetime would need a process that never runs its main loop at all, which quit() does not provide.

Only connect()-time CONNECT_DEFERRED is tested, not the alternative call_deferred("emit_signal", ...) form (deferring the emit call itself rather than the delivery). Both are expected to behave the same way (queued until the next frame) but only one form is verified here.
